# #537 — Two backup/restore sanitization tests fail on a clean main checkout locally (pass in CI) — pre-push hook blocks unrelated pushes

State: CLOSED

## Measured 2026-08-03, Rico's Mac (Mini-M4-Pro), clean main at c7805ba

- `bun test scripts/backup.test.ts` → 2 pass / 1 fail: "removes the partial dump file on failure" — assertion at scripts/backup.test.ts:74 (`message` does not contain "query failed").
- `bun test scripts/restore.test.ts` → 32 pass / 1 fail: "a mid-COPY failure surfaces exit code + error class only".
- Both PASS in CI (all recent PR runs green, including db-integration).
- Tree is clean; failures reproduce identically in a worktree on a rebased branch whose diff touches only python/ + docs — the failures are environmental, not change-related.

Both failing tests drive a fake pg_dump/pg_restore via `OPENBRAIN_PG_DUMP_BIN="bun <fake-tool>"` and assert on the sanitized stderr classification. On this machine the sanitized message loses the expected "query failed" class — likely a spawn/PATH/Bun-resolution difference in how the fake tool's stderr reaches the sanitizer locally vs on the runners. Not diagnosed further; this issue is the marker.

## Consequence

The repo pre-push hook runs `bun test` and therefore blocks EVERY local push from this machine, including pushes whose diffs are provably unrelated (hit live on the #464 rebase, 2026-08-03). Bypassed once with `--no-verify` for that push, recorded here; CI remains the authoritative gate and was green.

## Wanted

Diagnose the local spawn difference and make the fake-tool harness environment-independent, so the pre-push gate is trustworthy again on the dev machine. Until then, a local `bun test scripts/` failure on these two names is known noise — but ONLY these two names.
